GEORGE SOROS 

Why is billionaire George Soros a bogeyman for the hard right?

He's a Jewish multi-billionaire philanthropist who has given away $32bn. Why does the hard right from America to Australia and from Hungary to Honduras believe George Soros is at the heart of a global conspiracy, asks the BBC's Mike Rudin.

One quiet Monday afternoon last October in leafy upstate New York, a large manila envelope was placed in the mailbox of an exclusive country mansion belonging to multi-billionaire philanthropist George Soros.

The package looked suspicious. The return address was misspelt as "FLORIDS" and the mail had already been delivered earlier that day. The police were called and soon the FBI was on the scene.

Inside the bubble-wrapped envelope was a photograph of Soros, marked with a red "X". Alongside it, a six-inch plastic pipe, a small clock, a battery, wiring and a black powder.

More than a dozen similar packages were sent to the homes of former President Barack Obama, former Secretary of State Hillary Clinton and other prominent Democrats.

None of the devices exploded. The FBI traced the bombs to a white van covered in pro-Trump and anti-Democrat stickers, parked in a supermarket car park in Florida.

Immediately the right-wing media claimed it was a "false-flag" operation intended to derail President Donald Trump and the Republican campaign, just two weeks before the crucial US mid-term elections.

Fox Business host Lou Dobbs tweeted: "Fake News - Fake Bombs. Who could possibly benefit by so much fakery?" Conservative talk radio host Rush Limbaugh added: "Republicans just don't do this kind of thing."

Soon the internet was awash with allegations that the bomb plot was a hoax organized by Soros himself.

So how did George Soros come to be regarded by so many as the evil mastermind at the heart of a global conspiracy?

In the UK, Soros is known as "the man who broke the Bank of England" in 1992. Along with other currency speculators, he borrowed pounds, and then sold them, helping to drive down the price of sterling on currency markets and ultimately forcing the UK to crash out of the European Exchange Rate Mechanism. In the process he made $1bn.

The #Hungarian emigre, who survived the Holocaust and fled the Communists, is thought to have made in total about $44bn through financial speculation. And he's used his fortune to fund thousands of education, health, human rights and democracy projects.

Established in 1979, his Open Society Foundations now operate in more than 120 countries around the world. But this bold philanthropy in support of liberal, democratic causes has increasingly made him the bogeyman of the right.

The first conspiracy theories about George Soros appeared in the early 1990s, but they really gained traction after he condemned the 2003 Iraq War and started donating millions of dollars to the US Democratic Party.

Eight months into Trump's presidency, in August 2017, neo-Nazis held a torchlit procession in Charlottesville, Virginia. Clashes with counter-protesters ended in tragedy, when a white supremacist drove a car into a crowd and killed 32-year-old Heather Heyer.

Among US right-wingers it was soon claimed that the violence was orchestrated and financed by Soros, in order to tarnish the reputation of President Trump. And they said the key to the secret plot was a man called Brennan Gilmore, who filmed the car being driven into the counter-protesters. 

Right-wing radio host Alex Jones claimed Gilmore was paid $320,000 a year by Soros and was part of a deep-state coup to oust the president.

While it's true that Soros gave $500,000 to the political campaign of Tom Perriello - a Democratic candidate for governor of #Virginia whom Gilmore had worked for - there's no evidence Soros or the Open Society directed or paid protesters at Charlottesville. Gilmore, who never received any money from Soros, is now suing Alex Jones and several others for defamation.

The vilification of George Soros has spread far beyond the US, to Armenia, Australia, Honduras, the Philippines, Russia and many other countries.

Turkish Prime Minister Recep Tayyip Erdogan has accused Soros of being at the heart of a Jewish conspiracy to "divide" and "shatter" Turkey and other nations.

In Italy, former deputy prime minister Matteo Salvini accused him of wanting to fill the country with migrants because "he likes slaves".

The leader of the UK's Brexit Party, Nigel Farage, has claimed Soros is "actively encouraging people… to flood Europe" and "in many ways is the biggest danger to the entire Western World".

A lot of you haven't seen me in awhile because I stopped paying for X (there was a sex joke in there but I'm too tired to make it).

Anyway, let me just discuss this whole @IntersectMBO #Cardano constitution thing. 

Warning: It's going to be a long post.

Many of you that only follow me for my shitposts don't know what I've been doing for the past year. 

I moved to South Korea this year. Got married to my long time, long distance girlfriend and am now a resident (not citizen) of the country. Yes, a happy year... but it's not all candy and rainbows.

One of the reasons I finally decided to move is because of all the money I've lost being rugged in this space. 

While I'm thankfully not broke yet, after all the rugs and the expenses during the prior years dealing with my grandmother's illness, I have no savings left and covered 90% of the wedding expenses out of pocket. 

Mind you, this is only the Philippine side of the wedding. 

International weddings are usually 2 parts, so thankfully my wife is quite well off (compared to me anyway), so her and her family covered the South Korean side of the wedding.

But anyway, this is part of the reason for the move. The wealth gap in the Philippines between the have and have-nots has grown exponentially and salaries have not. 

I was already working like 2-3 odd jobs back in Manila and was barely making ends meet. And I'm supposed to be "middle-class". Moved here quitting all my jobs to start over and hopefully earn a livable wage again when I was finally contacted by Intersect that I seemed like a good fit for holding the Cardano Constitutional Workshop in the Philippines. An odd time to be sure as I got the email the week of my move to South Korea 😂

Considering the amount of work I put into trying to onboard people into Cardano with Christmas pies baked with the Cardano logo, Cardano logos on my part time catering business, and even having businesses I help set up with a reminder that "we accept ADA", and how I would constantly nag people for 3 years about how Cardano can change the world, I thought "finally, my efforts are paying off". But I wasn't going to be living in the Philippines anymore.

I explained to Intersect that I was no longer based in Manila so I would need to get a flight back just to host the workshop. They gave me a budget to work with and asked if it was possible to do it. I ran a few calculations and called several people back home to ask for a bunch of favors and realized the budget would fit + I might even get a small bonus if the price of ADA goes up, so I agreed to it.

Then come the payment terms for the workshop funding...

It was not unreasonable, but came out of left field. Payment would be in $ADA which I kind of expected but it would be paid in cycles. 

Half would be provided to me after I put up all the ads and got attendees (people still seemed excited about this so that seemed easy enough) but the other half would be upon completion of the workshop. Considering that venues and caterers want to be paid upfront (pretty common practice), this means I would once again be paying half the cost upfront. I understand of course where Intersect is coming from where they've never worked for me and want to see some output before funding anything but FFS, I don't have that kind of money on me. I even sent the receipts and billing statements from the venue and the caterer so they knew I wasn't making up prices to rip them off. But that wasn't enough. It had to be fair for all.

And I understand that. Fair for all is why I signed up for Cardano. So I made it work. I took up some debt and sold some ADA to pay off the venue and caterers for the workshop. The workshop itself was a bit of a nightmare (67 signups, 10 attendees) but that's a different story altogether. Sadly, the local Cardano community did not show support that day. And I ran ads on everything from FB to Instagram (except tiktok). Imagine having food prepared for up to 80 people and having 10 people show up! Could have used the money on something else IMO. FFS...

On the plus side, since none of our other members showed up, I was by default the only "expert" on Cardano governance and got selected as delegate.

Workshop ended on October 12 and I submitted the "deliverables" or basically the proof it happened the next day. Couldn't fake this shit anyway as an Intersect hired employee oversaw the whole thing (because we expected 60+ attendees, not 10). I got the other half of my funding a week after the workshop but ADA was down that day and I still had to pay my ground team and assistants so I sold it as I got it. Basically, I didn't make any money on hosting that workshop... But I'm not here to make money. I'm here to support our community, so fuck it. It's fine.

So by October 19, I began asking when visa processing would start. As "ANY" citizen from the 3rd world can tell you, it can take months to get a visa when you live in a developing country.

Radio silence.

Then a flood of emails the next week.

Delegates are expected to attend the workshop in Costa Rica on the first week of November or in Kenya on the 9th and 10th (both of which will require visas to enter if you don't have a "first world" passport). Thankfully they were not as strict for IRL attendance because of the visa issues for many delegates, but we were still required to attend and participate in these workshops online, followed by another required workshop on the 16th of November. 

I can only speak for myself on this part, but these 3 workshops were at 1 am to 9 am, 3 pm to 1 am, and 9 om to 2 pm respectively in Korean time. A terrible inconvenience when I should already be job hunting in Korea. 

Also, do you know how difficult it is to contribute to discussions when every workshop is basically when you're usually asleep or trying to find work?

Probably not because many of the "developed nation" delegates were asking if they could include their families in the intersect flight payments while us "undeveloped nation" delegates were happy just to represent the community and push governance forward.

Throughout this whole process, I kept bringing up how we should be prioritizing the visa processing of 3rd world delegates and just kept being told it was under control or that they had a team working on it. 

This was a stupid amount of stress for me who already had job hunting on his plate in order to support myself and my new family, coupled with getting emails at 3 am that I "had to answer ASAP" to facilitate the visa process.

It's been a nightmare having the expectations of my in-laws wondering what I'm going to do for work now that I've left my jobs in the Philippines, while simultaneously telling my wife I can't come to bed yet at 1 am because I need to finish this workshop (that I don't get paid for) because I need to support my community.

Mind you, Visa processing fees is 200 USD and intersect was only offering 250 USD compensation for travel and visa expenses in total before I complained about it (it's fixed now, or maybe it's not. IDK)

So again, more money out of pocket to work for free for Cardano governance where no one is even listening to the "developing nation" delegates about the difficulty of getting a visa FOR "developing nations".

Because I'm from a developing nation, I knew the difficulty of such things and I was already making strides to process the visa on my own and was just awaiting the documentation needed (more free fucking labor on my end), then on the day I get the invitation letter after I already got visa photos, booked a flight to the embassy (to get things moving) and was prepared to move, I'm told at 1 am the next morning to cease all processing because it's not happening anymore.

JFC!

All this could have been avoided if visa processing started over a month ago! (like I kept bringing up to everyone to the sound of crickets).

So now I've basically been wasting money, time and effort while disappointing my wife and looking like a bum to her family (now my family), and for what?!

If the "alternative plan" is to just "call in" my vote, you can forget it.

They won't even release the updated constitution to the public because the community "isn't ready" to see it yet, but somehow will be ready a week away from signing it when no more objections can be made, and no one listens to the concerns of the "developing nation" delegates who now cannot even speak to the other delegates in Argentina.

This is govenance? This is what I've been fighting for?!

Yeah, GL.
